meta.scope: Suriname batch 3 (final) — Fiscal/oil-revenue outlook, local content, social protection, exchange rate, and remaining trade/industrial nodes. Completes solid intermediate coverage for the final South America country.

candidates.title: Oil and mining fiscal revenues
candidates.description: Fiscal revenues from onshore oil, gold and (prospectively) offshore oil. Current backbone of public finances; Block 58 expected to produce a step-change from ~2028.
candidates.notes: Core fiscal-revenue node. Continuously cited in budget and sustainability analysis; the design of future oil-revenue management (including any sovereign fund) is a central policy debate.

candidates.title: Local content expectations for Block 58
candidates.description: Local-content commitments and expectations attached to the GranMorgu / Block 58 development (order of USD 1 bn local-content component cited in project descriptions).
candidates.notes: Spillover-policy node. Continuously cited as the main channel through which the offshore project is expected to generate domestic employment and enterprise beyond pure fiscal revenue.

candidates.title: Exchange rate / monetary conditions
candidates.description: Exchange-rate and monetary-policy indicators. High inflation and exchange-rate pressure defined the early-2020s crisis; stabilisation remains ongoing.
candidates.notes: Lived price and monetary signal. Continuously cited alongside inflation as the central stabilisation challenge of the post-crisis period.

candidates.title: Social protection and transfers
candidates.description: Social-protection programmes and transfers aimed at poverty and vulnerability reduction. Coverage and design are under pressure from fiscal constraints and high inflation.
candidates.notes: Lived safety-net node. Continuously cited in poverty and equity analysis; future oil revenues are widely expected to expand fiscal space for stronger social protection.

candidates.title: Merchandise trade statistics
candidates.description: Exports and imports of goods. Export basket dominated by gold and oil; imports reflect consumption, intermediate goods and (prospectively) large project-related capital goods.
candidates.notes: Primary high-frequency trade product. Gold and oil account for the large majority of export value.

candidates.title: District Wanica — coastal peri-urban
candidates.description: Coastal district adjacent to Paramaribo. Second major population concentration and peri-urban expansion area.
candidates.notes: Completes the greater Paramaribo statistical geography. Continuously appears among the largest population districts.

candidates.title: District Brokopondo — interior hydro and Maroon
candidates.description: Interior district with major hydroelectric infrastructure and large Maroon population share. Intermediate between deep interior and coastal zones.
candidates.notes: Interior energy and identity node. Completes the set of major interior districts alongside Sipaliwini.

candidates.title: IMF-supported stabilisation programme
candidates.description: IMF-supported macroeconomic stabilisation and reform programme that has framed fiscal, monetary and structural policy since the early-2020s crisis.
candidates.notes: External policy-anchor node. Continuously cited as the framework for post-crisis stabilisation pending the arrival of offshore oil revenues.

candidates.title: Agriculture, forestry and fisheries
candidates.description: Agriculture, forestry and fisheries production and employment. Smaller share of GDP than mining but material for rural livelihoods.
candidates.notes: Non-extractive primary sector. Continuously cited in diversification and rural-livelihood analysis.

candidates.title: Electricity access and generation
candidates.description: Electricity generation, access and reliability. National access is high on the coast; interior districts (especially Sipaliwini) have very low grid connection rates.
candidates.notes: Basic-services node. Coastal access is relatively high; interior access is a defining gap (Sipaliwini grid connection often cited near 30%).

proposed_edges.basis: Fiscal oil revenues originate primarily from Staatsolie operations and participating interests.
Local-content commitments are attached to the Block 58 / GranMorgu development.
Exchange-rate movements are a primary pass-through channel into consumer prices.
Social-protection transfers are designed to mitigate monetary poverty and vulnerability.
Merchandise trade is the primary goods component of the balance of payments.
The IMF programme frames debt and stabilisation policy.
Electricity access gaps are most severe in the interior districts.
Wanica forms the principal peri-urban extension of the greater Paramaribo area.
